summary: Halifax City Council has approved a broad infrastructure reinvestment plan covering roads, bridges, public transit, public buildings, digital systems and urban greenery. Projects include Bayers Road upgrades, the Green Overpass, an eco-friendly bus fleet, Central Library and City Hall renovations, Honore Bridge, smart street lights and an Urban Forest Initiative. The article presents the plan as positioning Halifax as a model of sustainable, contemporary urban development.
one_line: Halifax City Council approves a sweeping sustainable infrastructure plan spanning roads, transit, bridges, public buildings, smart city technology and urban forestry.
key_facts: On October 15, the Halifax City Council approved a resolution setting aside funds to rehabilitate outdated roads.
Bayers Road will get wider lanes plus dedicated bike lanes and pedestrian pathways; Councilor Maria Gonzalez of the Infrastructure Committee wants it to serve drivers, cyclists and walkers alike.
The Green Overpass project is set to break ground in November, serving as a connector between rapidly developing suburbs and a symbol of sustainability.
Councilor Johnathan Lee leads the eco-friendly bus fleet and bus depot upgrades, announced at a council meeting on September 20, with a projected completion date of mid-2024.
Work will soon begin on a light rail system; Councilor Linda Singh believes it will foster stronger community ties and faster transit.

Central Library renovations are scheduled to start in early 2024, focused on multipurpose spaces using natural light and energy-efficient systems; the redesign is by Miguel Hernandez of Miguel Hernandez Architecture.
City Hall, a historic landmark, will be restored to preserve its heritage while modernizing internal systems to meet environmental standards, per Emma Richards of the Heritage Committee.

Honore Bridge will connect the commercial district to East Halifax, with solar collection systems and eco-friendly materials; construction should start in early 2024 once regulatory hurdles are cleared.
Council member Andre Dupont said of Honore Bridge: "This bridge stands as proof of what can be accomplished when technology meets vision."
Susan Cho, Head of Digital Infrastructure Taskforce, unveiled a smart street-light project using networked LED lights with sensors that adjust lighting to pedestrian and vehicular traffic.
Plans also include intelligent traffic systems and public Wi-Fi zones as part of smart city upgrades.

The Urban Forest Initiative passed unanimously on December 6, featuring new parklands, tree planting and a 'green canopy' over the city; Environmental Planner Alice Munroe described it as building a legacy.
The overall plan aims to upgrade roads, bridges and public buildings across the region by September 2023.
